origin.author: Jason Allred
origin.raw_text: “What I have is almost a blog. A collection of ideas that I noticed actually started to work. But measuring is hard. How do I describe a cognitive jump? It's more like a strategy guide that worked really well, applied on several levels, and connecting it to a loop allows me to have complex conversations about things only cloud models could talk about. I guess the idea is that cloud models are good like savants with huge memory, but all we need is to design a hippocampus and connect it to a prefontal cortex. What I have are practical notes on building that.

Automatic indexes. Bringing intuition to the outside world beyond coding would need something similar - something to pop up critical context just in time. Refinement: Refine pearls rather than duplicate ideas. Provide a flow to Blend new ideas together. Providing flows - back pressure feedback loops. Building up complex flows with pearls as building blocks - gives bones to give structure and coherence. JITC is ambient, just in time, and just the relevant information at the right time. origin.author: Jason Allred
origin.raw_text: When using agents to code, long context becomes a problem. Agents start forgetting passive directives and enter an unpredictable phase that I like to describe as manic behavior. I tend to trust an agent as far as their kv cache lasts. This isn’t a new problem; adding more memory, kv cache optimizations, quantization, context compression, and RAG are all novel and interesting ways to enable stability over long context windows. The problem gets worse as projects grow, AGENTS.md expands and skills and tools are stacked on. The bloat is real and palatable, soon it’s possible to consume thousands of tokens just to answer a simple question. At some point it’s necessary to save the work that was done and start a fresh new session.

origin.author: Jason Allred
origin.raw_text: What local models _do_ have is offline access to personal data. Personal data is intimately tied to local models, many users specifically turn to local models to avoid pushing personal data to the cloud, to keep things in-house. There are also advantages to keeping things local: we can pre-process data offline. Filtering and database access is easy and fast.

origin.author: Jason Allred
origin.raw_text: Cloud models can use cache as a database, but local models don’t have that luxury or capacity. With local models the context problem turns into a data retrieval problem. We have already solved data retrieval years ago. Modern tools like ClaraDB, grep, RAG, Infinite Context Memory, and Claude memory blend the solutions that worked for humans into something that LLM Agents can use. When buying more memory is not practical, I propose a move to the extreme other end by shrinking context. How far can we focus the context to only relevant information to answer those simple questions? What can we do with small models and limited kv cache on desktop hardware that normally need God tier cloud power to answer?
